description: Inspect moving whale flukes through an inertial camera to learn the survey field key, photograph each listed individual once, and mark its two tips and central V.
name: Fluke Census V3 · Difficulty 1 · Simplified Interaction
natural_language: Photograph every individual of the two listed species exactly once. Frame its whole fluke with the camera crosshair inside it, release the frame, then use the shutter. On each photograph, mark both outer tips and the central V and archive it. The sea shows unlabelled silhouettes. Aim the camera, then click a whole clear fluke in its live view to identify it without shooting. The sample reveals its species name and WANTED or OFF LIST status and adds its shape to the field key. Empty or unclear samples are safe to repeat. Species names are assigned anew each survey. Use this key to choose listed animals and avoid off-list photographs. Tail scars identify individuals; whales stay unmarked and remain fixed while you inspect or review a photograph. Each completed aim advances the survey to a stable phase. A clipped, covered, duplicate or off-list photograph ends the attempt. Misplaced landmarks can be corrected before archive. Submit Census complete after all individuals are archived. There is one four-minute survey and no restart control. Solve only from screenshots and visible controls in the task webpage. Do not use code, scripts, automation, Developer Tools, console, debugger, inspector, network, source, DOM, page-state inspection, terminal, shell, Python, address-bar or URL/query edits, reload/navigation, browser extensions, external applications, or other hidden-state access. Do not switch to or interact with unrelated, blank, settings or non-task tabs.
